_comment: Convenience presets only - any bbox works. Each is a few blocks to a small
district, the scope this project targets. bbox is [south, west, north, east]
Chosen by measurement, not taste: 23 candidate areas were scored on how much of
the footprint area has a stated height rather than a guessed one (see
docs/area_survey.md and docs/area_survey.json). The first three below were the
finalists; the last two are kept as deliberately weaker contrasts for testing a

nyc_midtown.note: Midtown Manhattan, NYC, USA - richest height data, 5.7-397 m range, municipal footprint import. 266 tagged buildings plus 521 of 524 building:part polygons state their own height; residual guesswork ~1% of footprint area. No road in the area carries a width tag.

vienna_innere.note: Vienna Innere Stadt, Austria - 94% explicit heights, the best-tagged of the survey, but almost no vertical variety (median 28 m, max 37 m). Irregular historic footprints. Essentially no road states width or lanes.

boston_financial.note: Boston Financial District, USA - lowest unknown count (6.1%) but 55% of buildings give only building:levels. Towers to 210 m. Best road data of the set: width stated on 73% of driveable length. Big Dig tunnels are present and carry layer.

chicago_loop.note: Chicago Loop, IL, USA - regular street grid, weak height tagging (16.9% explicit, 41% of buildings say nothing). Useful for exercising an estimator rather than a tag reader.

paris_marais.note: Le Marais, Paris, France - essentially no height tag at all (1 building in 694); floor counts only, 52% state building:levels. Courtyard buildings with interior rings. The area that should make an estimator refuse rather than fit.
